title: The Sluice Hag's Rising Cave
story: Deep in a moonlit sea cave, Voulmirren the Sluice Hag cranks her great bone bellows and floods the cavern for fun. Three otter-folk pups are huddled on a stone ledge 24 inches above the water. Mr 6 plants his sword in the sand, sets his village's little pump churning, and starts counting instead of panicking.
question: The Hag's bellows raises the water 7.5 inches every minute, while Mr 6's pump drains 4.5 inches every minute. How many minutes until the water reaches the pups' ledge?
solution: Each minute the water really climbs 7.5 - 4.5 = 3 inches.
The ledge is 24 inches up, so the time is 24 / 3 = 8.
Mr 6 has 8 minutes to reach the pups.
praise: Working with the rate was exactly the right instinct — the missing step was subtracting the pump before dividing.
hint: The water is going up AND being pumped down at the same time. What is the water's real gain in one minute?
victory: Mr 6 carried all three pups out with a full minute to spare, then handed Voulmirren the pump handle so she could see how it felt. She flooded her own boots and fled, squelching, into the tide.
imagePrompt: A knightly numeral six with a blue cape braced in a moonlit sea cave, water swirling around his legs as a barnacled hag cranks a giant bone bellows and three otter pups cling to a high stone ledge.
